newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES REACH AGREEMENT WITH FREE AGENT HURLER WELLS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES REACH AGREEMENT WITH FREE AGENT HURLER WELLS.

text.p: The World Series champion New York Yankees began filling the holes in their pitching staff Tuesday as they reached agreement in principle with free agent left-hander David Wells.

The team issued a one-sentence press release saying they have reached an agreement with Wells -- reportedly for three years at about $15 million -- but had not yet resolved contract language and luxury tax issues.

Wells, 33, posted an 11-14 record with an unimpressive 5.14 earned run average in 34 starts last season with the Baltimore Orioles. Wells, however, enjoys pitching in Yankee Stadium where he owns a 10-1 lifetime record.

New York had already lost starting pitcher Jimmy Key to Baltimore and closer John Wetteland to the Texas Rangers through free agency. Wells would be the third left-hander on a starting rotation that features Andy Pettitte, David Cone, Dwight Gooden and Kenny Rogers.
In the playoffs this season, Wells went 2-0 with a 4.43 ERA in three starts. He gave Baltimore their only win against the Yankees in the American League Championship Series.
Despite the fact Wells was born in Torrance, California, he has always been a Yankees fan and during the league championship series, talked about his his special feeling competing in Yankee Stadium.
"I always dreamed about being in Yankee Stadium as a kid," said Wells, who has a career record of 90-75. "Coming here and knowing the history, it's something special."
